001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.util.HashMap;
004import java.util.Map;
005import java.util.Objects;
006import java.util.function.BiConsumer;
007
008import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
009
010import io.jstach.rainbowgum.KeyValues.MutableKeyValues;
011
012/**
013 * Key Value Pairs similar to a {@code Map<String,String>} but optimized for memory and
014 * less garbage (no iterators).
015 * <p>
016 * The observed order of the current default Key Value Pairs is insertion based ordering
017 * but that should not be relied on as other implementations may change that.
018 * <p>
019 * The preferred way to get all or most of the key values out for formatting is to use
020 * {@link KeyValuesConsumer}. There is deliberately no low-level, index-based access
021 * (something like {@code key(int)}/{@code valueOrNull(int)}) on this interface: that
022 * shape only makes sense for an array-backed implementation, and would force every
023 * implementation - including ones not backed by a flat array - to expose it anyway.
024 *
025 * @apiNote The current key values implementation is a simple single String array as the
026 * assumption is that most MDC (and or addKeyValuePair) usage is for a couple values and
027 * that many formatting usages particularly JSON or headers are to retrieve
028 * <strong>all</strong> of the key values. Another assumption for the simplicity is to
029 * save memory as there is a potential for many KeyValues with the advent of virtual
030 * threads and key values cannot be escaped analysis or garbage collected quickly because
031 * they are passed all the way down to the output.
032 * <p>
033 * The unfortunate consequence of this is that ad-hoc single key lookup or removal is
034 * <code>O(n)</code> and not <code>O(1)</code>. If you find this unacceptable with
035 * benchmarking because of having many keys and only retrieving a few please file an issue
036 * and we may offer alternative map or binary tree implementations in the future.
037 */
038public sealed interface KeyValues {
039
040        /**
041         * Analogous to {@link Map#get(Object)}
042         * @param key key never <code>null</code>.
043         * @return value for key maybe <code>null</code>.
044         */
045        public @Nullable String getValueOrNull(String key);
046
047        /**
048         * Used to easily iterate over the key value pairs without using an iterator.
049         * @param action consumer called on each key value pair.
050         */
051        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
052        void forEach(BiConsumer<? super String, ? super @Nullable String> action);
053
054        /**
055         * Used to easily iterate over the key value pairs without using an iterator.
056         * @param <V> storage type
057         * @param action consumer.
058         * @param counter a pass through integer that can be used for counting purposes or
059         * determining the start perhaps by passing <code>0</code> and then incrementing on
060         * return.
061         * @param storage an extra parameter to avoid unnecessary lambda creation.
062         * @return new value for next counter to be passed to {@link KeyValuesConsumer}.
063         * {@link KeyValuesConsumer#accept(KeyValues, String, String, int, Object)} return.
064         */
065        <V> int forEach(KeyValues.KeyValuesConsumer<V> action, int counter, V storage);
066
067        /**
068         * An immutable empty {@link KeyValues}.
069         * @return immutable empty {@link KeyValues}.
070         */
071        static KeyValues of() {
072                return EmptyKeyValues.INSTANCE;
073        }
074
075        /**
076         * Analogous to {@link Map#size()}.
077         * @return size.
078         */
079        int size();
080
081        /**
082         * Analogous to {@link Map#isEmpty()}.
083         * @return true if empty.
084         */
085        default boolean isEmpty() {
086                return size() <= 0;
087        }
088
089        /**
090         * A special consumer that avoids lambda garbage.
091         *
092         * @param <V> storage
093         */
094        interface KeyValuesConsumer<V> {
095
096                /**
097                 * Accepts the KeyValues at the current key and value.
098                 * @param kvs kvs.
099                 * @param k key.
100                 * @param v value.
101                 * @param index counter.
102                 * @param storage storage like a StringBuidler.
103                 * @return custom user count that will be accumulated. If one was returned for
104                 * each call then the result would be the total count.
105                 */
106                public int accept(KeyValues kvs, String k, @Nullable String v, int index, V storage);
107
108        }
109
110        /**
111         * Creates an immutable key values by copying a Map.
112         * @param m map.
113         * @return immutable key values.
114         * @apiNote Be careful when use {@link Map#of()} as its order is non deterministic
115         * because most map implementations are and thus the resulting key values may not be
116         * in the order you expect.
117         */
118        public static KeyValues of(Map<String, String> m) {
119                if (m.isEmpty())
120                        return of();
121                ArrayKeyValues mdc = new ArrayKeyValues(m.size());
122                mdc.putAll(m);
123                return mdc.freeze();
124        }
125
126        /**
127         * Creates a key values whose entries are the union of two key values, {@code high}
128         * taking precedence over {@code low} on a key collision. The result is an eagerly
129         * built, immutable copy: {@code low} and {@code high} are read once, at the moment of
130         * this call, and are not retained or delegated to afterward. Multiple layers merge by
131         * nesting, e.g. {@code merge(merge(a, b), c)}, the same way a cons list nests -
132         * {@code c} wins over {@code b}, which wins over {@code a}.
133         * @param low lower precedence key values.
134         * @param high higher precedence key values, wins on key collision.
135         * @return {@code high} if {@code low} is empty, {@code low} if {@code high} is empty,
136         * otherwise an immutable copy of both merged together.
137         */
138        public static KeyValues merge(KeyValues low, KeyValues high) {
139                if (low.isEmpty()) {
140                        return high;
141                }
142                if (high.isEmpty()) {
143                        return low;
144                }
145                return mergeArrays(low, high);
146        }
147
148        /*
149         * low's own keys are already unique (a KeyValues never carries a duplicate), so its
150         * entries never need putKeyValue's duplicate scan the way high's do - only high can
151         * actually collide with what low already contributed. When low is a dense (gap-free)
152         * array-backed KeyValues - true for essentially everything that reaches here in
153         * practice, since merge()'s own output is always dense and neither KeyValues.of(Map)
154         * nor ScopedKeyValues.Builder ever call remove() - its entries are bulk-copied
155         * straight into the new backing array via System.arraycopy rather than appended one
156         * at a time, which is what actually gets this close to a HashMap copy's own cost
157         * rather than just skipping the duplicate scan. A low that is not known dense falls
158         * back to ArrayKeyValues#appendUnchecked (still no duplicate scan, just per-entry
159         * instead of one bulk copy) since a raw copy could otherwise stop at a gap before
160         * reaching real entries that come after it.
161         */
162        private static KeyValues mergeArrays(KeyValues low, KeyValues high) {
163                ArrayKeyValues buf = new ArrayKeyValues(low.size() + high.size());
164                buf.kvs = new @Nullable String[buf.threshold];
165                if (low instanceof AbstractArrayKeyValues low2 && low2.dense) {
166                        System.arraycopy(low2.kvs, 0, buf.kvs, 0, low2.size * 2);
167                        buf.size = low2.size;
168                }
169                else {
170                        low.forEach(buf::appendUnchecked);
171                }
172                high.forEach(buf);
173                return buf.freeze();
174        }
175
176        /**
177         * Copies the KeyValues to a Map. This should be used sparingly.
178         * @return map of kvs.
179         */
180        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
181        Map<String, @Nullable String> copyToMap();
182
183        /**
184         * Makes the KeyValues thread safe either by copying or returning if already
185         * immutable.
186         * @return immutable key values.
187         */
188        public KeyValues freeze();
189
190        /**
191         * KeyValues that can be updated.
192         */
193        public sealed interface MutableKeyValues extends KeyValues, BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> {
194
195                /**
196                 * Copies.
197                 * @return kvs copy.
198                 */
199                MutableKeyValues copy();
200
201                /**
202                 * Same as {@link Map#put(Object, Object)}.
203                 * @param key key.
204                 * @param value value maybe <code>null</code>.
205                 */
206                void putKeyValue(String key, @Nullable String value);
207
208                /**
209                 * Fluent version of put.
210                 * @param key key.
211                 * @param value value maybe <code>null</code>.
212                 * @return this.
213                 */
214                default MutableKeyValues add(String key, @Nullable String value) {
215                        putKeyValue(key, value);
216                        return this;
217                }
218
219                /**
220                 * Same as {@link Map#remove(Object)}.
221                 * @param key key.
222                 */
223                void remove(String key);
224
225                /**
226                 * Same as {@link #putKeyValue(String, String)} but will ignore null keys from
227                 * sources that have null keys.
228                 */
229                @Override
230                default void accept(@Nullable String t, @Nullable String u) {
231                        if (t == null) {
232                                return;
233                        }
234                        putKeyValue(t, u);
235                }
236
237                /**
238                 * Same as {@link Map#putAll(Map)}.
239                 * @param m map.
240                 */
241                default void putAll(Map<String, ? extends @Nullable String> m) {
242                        m.forEach(this);
243                }
244
245                /**
246                 * Copies a map into {@link MutableKeyValues}.
247                 * @param m map.
248                 * @return key values
249                 */
250                public static MutableKeyValues of(Map<String, String> m) {
251                        int size = m.size();
252                        var kvs = of(size == 0 ? 4 : size);
253                        kvs.putAll(m);
254                        return kvs;
255                }
256
257                /**
258                 * Creates mutable keys with pre-allocation.
259                 * @param size should be greater than 0.
260                 * @return mutable keys.
261                 */
262                public static MutableKeyValues of(int size) {
263                        return new ArrayKeyValues(size);
264                }
265
266                /**
267                 * Empty mutable keys with default pre-allocation.
268                 * @return mutable keys.
269                 */
270                public static MutableKeyValues of() {
271                        return new ArrayKeyValues();
272                }
273
274        }
275
276        /**
277         * Pretty prints key values.
278         * @param kvs kvs.
279         * @param sb StringBuilder.
280         */
281        public static void prettyPrint(KeyValues kvs, StringBuilder sb) {
282                sb.append('{');
283                kvs.forEach(AbstractArrayKeyValues.toStringer, 0, sb);
284                sb.append('}');
285        }
286
287        /**
288         * Checks if two {@link KeyValues} are equal.
289         * @param self first.
290         * @param kvs second.
291         * @return true if equal.
292         */
293        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
294        static boolean equals(KeyValues self, KeyValues kvs) {
295                if (self == kvs)
296                        return true;
297                if (kvs.size() != self.size()) {
298                        return false;
299                }
300                boolean[] result = { true };
301                self.forEach((k, v) -> {
302                        if (result[0] && !Objects.equals(v, kvs.getValueOrNull(k))) {
303                                result[0] = false;
304                        }
305                });
306                return result[0];
307        }
308
309}

311final class EmptyKeyValues implements KeyValues {
312
313        static final EmptyKeyValues INSTANCE = new EmptyKeyValues();
314
315        private EmptyKeyValues() {
316        }
317
318        @Override
319        public @Nullable String getValueOrNull(String key) {
320                return null;
321        }
322
323        @Override
324        public void forEach(BiConsumer<? super String, ? super String> action) {
325        }
326
327        @Override
328        public <V> int forEach(KeyValuesConsumer<V> action, int index, V storage) {
329                return index;
330        }
331
332        @Override
333        public int size() {
334                return 0;
335        }
336
337        @Override
338        public Map<String, @Nullable String> copyToMap() {
339                return Map.of();
340        }
341
342        @Override
343        public KeyValues freeze() {
344                return this;
345        }
346
347        @Override
348        public boolean equals(@Nullable Object keyValues) {
349                if (keyValues instanceof KeyValues kvs) {
350                        return kvs.isEmpty();
351                }
352                return false;
353        }
354
355        @Override
356        public int hashCode() {
357                return 1;
358        }
359
360        @Override
361        public String toString() {
362                return "{}";
363        }
364
365}
366
367sealed abstract class AbstractArrayKeyValues implements KeyValues {
368
369        protected static final KeyValuesConsumer<StringBuilder> toStringer = (kvs, k, v, i, b) -> {
370                if (i > 0) {
371                        b.append(',').append(' ');
372                }
373                b.append('"').append(k).append('"').append(':').append('"').append(v).append('"');
374                return i + 1;
375        };
376
377        protected static final int DEFAULT_INITIAL_CAPACITY = 2;
378
379        protected static final String[] EMPTY = new String[] {};
380
381        protected @Nullable String[] kvs;
382
383        protected int size;
384
385        protected int threshold;
386
387        /*
388         * True as long as no MutableKeyValues#remove(String) has ever left a gap in kvs -
389         * KeyValues.merge's fast path bulk-copies another instance's raw kvs array via
390         * System.arraycopy only when this is true, since that skips the usual "stop at the
391         * first empty slot" scan and would otherwise risk stopping at a gap before reaching
392         * real entries that come after it. Defaults true (every fresh instance starts gap
393         * free) and is propagated by copy()/freeze() below, since those also copy kvs
394         * verbatim, gaps and all.
395         */
396        protected boolean dense = true;
397
398        protected AbstractArrayKeyValues(@Nullable String[] kvs, int size, int threshold) {
399                super();
400                this.kvs = kvs;
401                this.size = size;
402                this.threshold = threshold;
403        }
404
405        @Override
406        public int size() {
407                return this.size;
408        }
409
410        @Override
411        public @Nullable String getValueOrNull(String key) {
412                if (size == 0) {
413                        return null;
414                }
415                for (int i = 0; i < (threshold - 1); i += 2) {
416                        var k = kvs[i];
417                        /*
418                         * get
419                         */
420                        if (Objects.equals(k, key)) {
421                                return kvs[i + 1];
422                        }
423                }
424                return null;
425        }
426
427        @Override
428        public void forEach(BiConsumer<? super String, ? super @Nullable String> action) {
429                if (size == 0) {
430                        return;
431                }
432                for (int i = 0; i < (threshold - 1); i += 2) {
433                        var k = kvs[i];
434                        var v = kvs[i + 1];
435                        if (k == null) {
436                                continue;
437                        }
438                        action.accept(k, v);
439                }
440        }
441
442        @Override
443        public <V> int forEach(KeyValuesConsumer<V> action, int index, V storage) {
444                if (size == 0) {
445                        return index;
446                }
447                for (int i = 0; i < (threshold - 1); i += 2) {
448                        var k = kvs[i];
449                        var v = kvs[i + 1];
450                        if (k == null) {
451                                continue;
452                        }
453                        index = action.accept(this, k, v, index, storage);
454                }
455
456                return index;
457
458        }
459
460        @Override
461        public Map<String, @Nullable String> copyToMap() {
462                final Map<String, @Nullable String> result = new HashMap<>(size);
463                forEach(result::put);
464                return result;
465        }
466
467        @Override
468        public String toString() {
469                StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
470                KeyValues.prettyPrint(this, sb);
471                return sb.toString();
472        }
473
474        protected static int calculateInitialThreshold(final int initialCapacity) {
475                if (initialCapacity < 0) {
476                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Initial capacity must be at least zero but was " + initialCapacity);
477                }
478                return 2 * ceilingNextPowerOfTwo(initialCapacity == 0 ? 1 : initialCapacity);
479        }
480
481        /**
482         * Calculate the next power of 2, greater than or equal to x.
483         * <p>
484         * From Hacker's Delight, Chapter 3, Harry S. Warren Jr.
485         * @param x Value to round up
486         * @return The next power of 2 from x inclusive
487         */
488        protected static int ceilingNextPowerOfTwo(final int x) {
489                final int BITS_PER_INT = 32;
490                return 1 << (BITS_PER_INT - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(x - 1));
491        }
492
493        @Override
494        public int hashCode() {
495                int[] result = { 1 };
496                forEach((k, v) -> {
497                        result[0] = result[0] + k.hashCode();
498                        result[0] = result[0] + (v == null ? 0 : v.hashCode());
499                });
500                return result[0];
501        }
502
503        @Override
504        public boolean equals(@Nullable Object obj) {
505                if (obj instanceof KeyValues kvs) {
506                        return KeyValues.equals(this, kvs);
507                }
508                return false;
509        }
510
511}
512
513final class ImmutableArrayKeyValues extends AbstractArrayKeyValues {
514
515        @SuppressWarnings("null")
516        ImmutableArrayKeyValues(String[] kvs, int size, int threshold) {
517                super(kvs, size, threshold);
518        }
519
520        @Override
521        public KeyValues freeze() {
522                return this;
523        }
524
525}

527/*
528 * A KeyValues that uses a single string array for memory savings which is desirable in
529 * the case of loom where there could be several orders of key values instances at any
530 * given time.
531 */
532final class ArrayKeyValues extends AbstractArrayKeyValues implements MutableKeyValues {
533
534        public ArrayKeyValues() {
535                this(DEFAULT_INITIAL_CAPACITY);
536        }
537
538        @SuppressWarnings("null")
539        public ArrayKeyValues(final int initialCapacity) {
540                this(EMPTY, 0, calculateInitialThreshold(initialCapacity));
541        }
542
543        private ArrayKeyValues(@Nullable String[] kvs, int size, int threshold) {
544                super(kvs, size, threshold);
545                this.kvs = kvs;
546                this.size = size;
547                this.threshold = threshold;
548        }
549
550        @Override
551        public MutableKeyValues copy() {
552                if (size == 0) {
553                        return new ArrayKeyValues();
554                }
555                ArrayKeyValues orig = this;
556                @Nullable String[] copyKvs = new @Nullable String[this.threshold];
557                System.arraycopy(orig.kvs, 0, copyKvs, 0, orig.threshold);
558                var result = new ArrayKeyValues(copyKvs, size, threshold);
559                result.dense = this.dense;
560                return result;
561        }
562
563        @SuppressWarnings("null") // Eclipse bug
564        @Override
565        public KeyValues freeze() {
566                if (size == 0) {
567                        return KeyValues.of();
568                }
569                ArrayKeyValues orig = this;
570                String[] copyKvs = new String[this.threshold];
571                System.arraycopy(orig.kvs, 0, copyKvs, 0, orig.threshold);
572                var result = new ImmutableArrayKeyValues(copyKvs, size, threshold);
573                result.dense = this.dense;
574                return result;
575        }
576
577        public @Nullable String apply(String t) {
578                return getValueOrNull(t);
579        }
580
581        /*
582         * We implement BiConsumer to avoid garbage like entry set and iterators
583         */
584        @Override
585        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
586        public void putKeyValue(String key, @Nullable String value) {
587                Objects.requireNonNull(key);
588                if (kvs == EMPTY) {
589                        inflateTable(threshold);
590                }
591
592                for (int i = 0; i < (threshold - 1); i += 2) {
593                        var k = kvs[i];
594                        /*
595                         * replacement
596                         */
597                        if (Objects.equals(k, key)) {
598                                kvs[i + 1] = value;
599                                return;
600                        }
601                        else if (k == null && kvs[i + 1] == null) {
602                                kvs[i] = key;
603                                kvs[i + 1] = value;
604                                size++;
605                                return;
606                        }
607                }
608                ensureCapacity();
609                size++;
610                int valueIndex = (size * 2) - 1;
611                kvs[valueIndex - 1] = key;
612                kvs[valueIndex] = value;
613        }
614
615        /*
616         * putKeyValue's leading scan exists to find/overwrite an existing key, so calling it
617         * size() times to copy in an already-duplicate-free KeyValues costs 1+2+...+size()
618         * comparisons - O(size()^2). Skipping straight to the append tail is safe only when
619         * the caller already knows key cannot be a duplicate, e.g. copying another KeyValues'
620         * entries (unique by construction) one at a time into a buffer that started empty -
621         * used as KeyValues#merge's fallback for a low side that is not dense
622         * (System.arraycopy is unsafe there - see the `dense` field), which is otherwise the
623         * same shape as putKeyValue's own append tail.
624         */
625        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
626        void appendUnchecked(String key, @Nullable String value) {
627                if (kvs == EMPTY) {
628                        inflateTable(threshold);
629                }
630                ensureCapacity();
631                size++;
632                int valueIndex = (size * 2) - 1;
633                kvs[valueIndex - 1] = key;
634                kvs[valueIndex] = value;
635        }
636
637        @Override
638        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
639        public void remove(final String key) {
640                if (kvs == EMPTY) {
641                        return;
642                }
643                for (int i = 0; i < (threshold - 1); i += 2) {
644                        var k = kvs[i];
645                        /*
646                         * remove
647                         */
648                        if (Objects.equals(k, key)) {
649                                kvs[i] = null;
650                                kvs[i + 1] = null;
651                                size--;
652                                dense = false;
653                        }
654                }
655        }
656
657        private void ensureCapacity() {
658                if ((size * 2) >= threshold) {
659                        resize(threshold * 2);
660                }
661        }
662
663        private void resize(final int newCapacity) {
664                final @Nullable String[] oldKvs = kvs;
665
666                kvs = new @Nullable String[newCapacity];
667
668                System.arraycopy(oldKvs, 0, kvs, 0, (size * 2));
669
670                threshold = newCapacity;
671        }
672
673        /**
674         * Inflates the table.
675         */
676        private void inflateTable(final int toSize) {
677                threshold = toSize;
678                kvs = new @Nullable String[toSize];
679        }
680
681}
